        ### Question
        A 25-year-old man is brought to the emergency department 30 minutes after he was involved in a motorcycle collision. He was not wearing a helmet. Physical examination shows left periorbital ecchymosis. A CT scan of the head shows a fracture of the greater wing of the left sphenoid bone with compression of the left superior orbital fissure. Physical examination of this patient is most likely to show which of the following findings?

        ### Options
        opa. Decreased sense of smell
opb. Numbness of the left cheek
opc. Preserved left lateral gaze
opd. Absent left corneal reflex
ope. Complete loss of vision of the left eye

### Reasoning Chains per Option:
CHAIN: Fracture of the greater wing of the left sphenoid bone with compression of the left superior orbital fissure -> Impaired function of cranial nerve III, IV, and VI -> Possible ophthalmoplegia -> 80% CHAIN: Compression of the left superior orbital fissure -> Impaired function of cranial nerve VI (abducens nerve) -> Possible limitation in left lateral gaze -> 75% CHAIN: Fracture involving the left superior orbital fissure -> Potential damage to cranial nerve V1 (ophthalmic division of the trigeminal nerve) -> Possible absent left corneal reflex -> 70% CHAIN: Fracture affecting the left superior orbital fissure -> Potential optic nerve compression -> Possible complete loss of vision in the left eye -> 80%

### Retrieved Evidence Paths (broad but correct):
